The resulting non-convex optimization problem, which involves strongly coupled variables, is addressed using a graph neural network (GNN) that predicts the beamforming, polarization, and power-splitting variables. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed GNN-based dynamic polarforming optimization significantly outperforms fixed-polarization schemes, particularly under imperfect channel state information (CSI). Moreover, joint polarforming and GNN-based optimization maintains robust SWIPT performance under both polarization mismatch and imperfect CSI.
item.dc:creator: Hamed Aghaei-Karkaj, Kamran Ebrahimi, Zahra Mehrzad, Mohammad Robat Mili, Symeon Chatzinotas

item.title: Sum Rate Maximization for Practical RIS-Enhanced Rate-Splitting Multiple Access Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.14765v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) combined with rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) provide a promising solution for improving the spectral efficiency (SE) of sixth-generation (6G) communication systems. However, most existing studies neglect the practical coupling between the RIS phase shift and amplitude, which may cause phase-shift mismatch and significant performance loss. In this paper, we investigate the multiuser sum-rate maximization problem for practical RIS-enhanced RSMA systems considering amplitude-phase coupling. To address the resulting non-convex problem, an effective variable separation algorithm is proposed. The proposed algorithm is compatible with RIS reflecting optimization under the continuous phase shift or any amplitude-phase coupling relationship and can also be directly extended to practical RIS-enhanced NOMA and OMA systems. Simulation results demonstrate performance gain of over 190\% compared with the ideal-RIS-based benchmark, while the proposed RSMA scheme significantly outperforms the corresponding NOMA and OMA schemes.
item.dc:creator: Qian Zhang, Xuejun Cheng, Jiaming Shi, Yufei Zhao, Rugui Yao, Ye Fan

item.title: Precision Coexistence: Angular-Spectral Region Constrained Waveform Design for MIMO-ISAC
item.description: arXiv:2610.29364v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we develop a dual-function waveform design framework for multiple-input multiple-output integrated sensing and communication (MIMO-ISAC) systems operating in congested electromagnetic environments. In such environments, the dual-function waveform must coexist with legacy systems, such as localized positioning sensors, maritime radar networks, and satellite communication links, that occupy specific frequency bands and angular sectors. To enable precision coexistence, we incorporate localized angular-spectral region constraints that suppress beamformed energy only within the angle-frequency regions occupied by each legacy system, while preserving the spatial degrees of freedom (DoFs) available outside those regions. The resulting waveform design problem is formulated as a nonconvex optimization problem and solved using a low-complexity majorization--minimization alternating direction method of multipliers (MM--ADMM) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides precise legacy-system protection while maintaining robust radar sensing and multi-user communication performance.
item.dc:creator: Syed Ali Haider Shirazi, Taejoon Kim, David J. Love, Sergiy A. Vorobyov

item.title: Optimal Additive Integer Masks for One-Guess Vulnerability under an Absolute-Moment Budget
item.description: arXiv:2611.16066v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A defender releases an integer-valued secret $X$ (a count, a discretised measurement, a clock value) as $Y = X + N$, where $N$ is an independent integer-valued mask whose expected absolute value, the expected distortion of the released value, is at most $c$. An adversary who knows the prior of $X$ and the law of $N$ observes $Y$ once and makes a single guess. We determine exactly how small the adversary's success probability, the posterior Bayes vulnerability, can be made, and which masks achieve it. For a secret supported on an interval of $m$ integers we give the optimum and an explicit optimiser for the uniform prior; by the maximal-leakage formula, the same mask minimises the worst-case-prior one-guess leakage for every prior with that support. For a biased bit, the simplest prior a defender can exploit, we characterise the masks that leak nothing on average, give the critical budget at which this becomes possible, and determine the entire cost-vulnerability frontier. It is the piecewise-linear interpolation of an explicit sequence of points generated by cost-optimally shifted truncated geometric masks, with infinitely many affine pieces accumulating at the critical budget, where the frontier meets the prior vulnerability with zero slope. The proof rests on a layer-cake decomposition of an arbitrary mask into truncated geometrics, along which both vulnerability and cost are exactly additive. The results give exact, prior-aware design guidance for additive integer noise against one-guess adversaries.
item.dc:creator: Joonas P\"a\"akk\"onen

item.title: A tight upper bound on non-overlapping codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.21913v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Non-overlapping codes (also known as cross bifix-free codes or strong comma-free codes) have now been studied for over 60 years as part of information theory, with regular new applications appearing and much recent interest. Let $X$ be a $q$-ary non-overlapping code of length $n$. The paper contains a self-contained proof that \[ |X|\leq \left(\frac{q-1}{qe} +O(n^{-1/4})\right)\frac{q^n}{n} \] as $n\rightarrow\infty$ with $q$ fixed, where $e$ is the base of the natural logarithm. The constant $(q-1)/(qe)$ improves, by a factor of $(q-1)/q$, the best previously known bound due to Levenshtein (1970). Indeed, constructions of large non-overlapping codes show that this constant is best possible. The paper builds on work by Fimmel, Michel, Pirot, Sereni and Str\"ungmann (2019), and by Stanovnik, Mo\v skon and Mraz (2024).
item.dc:creator: Simon R. Blackburn

item.title: Asymptotic Bounds for Codes in Toroidal Distance
item.description: arXiv:2611.25990v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The toroidal distance naturally describes the geometry of codes over \(\mathbb Z_q\), where distances are measured modulo \(q\). In this paper, we study asymptotic bounds for codes in \(\mathbb Z_q^n\) under the toroidal metric. We first derive an explicit asymptotic lower bound from the classical Gilbert--Varshamov bounds for the Hamming and Lee metrics, which serves as a baseline for comparison. We then develop a saddle-point approach for the toroidal metric, which yields an asymptotic Gilbert--Varshamov lower bound and an asymptotic Hamming-type upper bound. For \(3\mid q\), we embed ternary Hamming codes into \(\mathbb Z_q^n\) and obtain another asymptotic lower bound for the toroidal metric. In addition, we derive an asymptotic lower bound for Maximum Toroidal Distance (MTD) codes. We compare these lower bounds with the baseline and prove that they are nontrivial in the corresponding parameter ranges. Finally, we compare the asymptotic bounds numerically.
item.dc:creator: Pengjie Zhong, Jinquan Luo

item.title: Channel coding against quantum jammers via minimax
item.description: arXiv:2505.11362v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study classical communication over fully quantum arbitrarily varying channels, in which a jammer can prepare an arbitrary state entangled across channel uses. We formulate assisted codes as joint input-output maps and apply Sion's minimax theorem to exchange optimization over codes and jamming states at fixed message size. Combining this reduction with one-shot coding bounds and a generalized quantum asymptotic equipartition property yields a single-letter formula for the entanglement-assisted classical capacity, a single-letter formula for the shared-randomness-assisted capacity of classical-quantum channels, and a regularized formula for general quantum input channels. For entanglement assistance and for shared-randomness-assisted classical-quantum channels, we extend the capacity formulas to arbitrary jammer Hilbert spaces while keeping the sender and receiver systems finite-dimensional. The extension uses finite-dimensional approximations at each blocklength, a uniform bound on the change in coding error, and compact closures of finite-dimensional output-state sets. These arguments avoid de Finetti reductions and establish equality with the corresponding compound-channel capacities in these two settings.
item.dc:creator: Michael X. Cao, Yongsheng Yao, Mario Berta

item.title: Distribution free M-estimation
item.description: arXiv:2505.22807v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The basic question of delineating those statistical problems that are solvable without making any assumptions on the underlying data distribution has long animated statistics and learning theory. This paper characterizes when a convex M-estimation or stochastic optimization problem is solvable in such an assumption-free setting, providing a precise dividing line between solvable and unsolvable problems. The conditions we identify show, perhaps surprisingly, that Lipschitz continuity of the loss being minimized is not necessary for distribution free minimization, and they are also distinct from classical characterizations of learnability in machine learning.
item.dc:creator: Felipe Areces, John C. Duchi

item.title: Industrial Viewpoints on RAN Technologies for 6G
item.description: arXiv:2508.08225v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Sixth-generation (6G) mobile systems have entered the standardization phase, with commercial deployments anticipated around 2030. This article presents an industrial perspective on the performance targets and key technologies shaping the 6G radio access network (RAN). It examines advances in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO), artificial intelligence (AI), waveforms, channel coding, signal constellations, integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), and the integration of terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks (NTNs). Although detailed specification work is still ahead, the scope of the 6G studies has been defined and substantial technical progress has been made. We assess the emerging technologies and design choices from the perspectives of implementation complexity, computational and energy efficiency, interoperability, deployment feasibility, and migration from 5G. By connecting research advances with practical standardization and commercialization considerations, this article aims to inform researchers and industry practitioners developing the 6G RAN.
item.dc:creator: Mansoor Shafi, Erik G. Larsson, Xingqin Lin, Dorin Panaitopol, Stefan Parkvall, Flavien Ronteix-Jacquet, Antti Toskala

item.title: From description to design: Automated engineering of complex systems with desirable emergent properties
item.description: arXiv:2603.15631v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Across the sciences, researchers have developed hundreds of statistics that describe the collective behavior of complex systems. These statistics are typically used passively, to describe a system after the fact, so it is rarely learned whether the patterns captured actually matter. The problem of engineering systems that display desirable emergent properties is a less developed area, as the very nature of emergent phenomena challenges the typical bottom-up approach to engineering. Here we propose a top-down approach, re-purposing the large number of descriptive statistics as objective functions in an optimization pipeline. Since this method lets a collective property instantiated directly, it makes long-standing correlational questions amenable to experimentation. We demonstrate this concept on four models taken from four different areas of science: a Kuramoto coupled-oscillator model (physics), a Wilson-Cowan network of excitatory and inhibitory processes (neuroscience), an SIRS pandemic spread model (epidemiology), and an echo-state network (machine learning). In each case, we take measures commonly used to describe behavior and feed those descriptive statistics back into the system to sculpt desirable macro-scale properties into the fundamental generative dynamics. We find that this approach is successful across domains and systems, and the inclusion of ``emergent" measures can actually improve the ability of some systems to perform tasks. We argue these threads can be unified into a general practice of emergent engineering that combines traditional task-oriented, bottom-up approaches to engineering with top-down guidance of collective, emergent properties to build resilient, capable, complex systems.
item.dc:creator: Thomas F. Varley, Josh Bongard

item.title: Polynomial-Time Optimal Group Selection via the Double-Commutator Eigenvalue Problem
item.description: arXiv:2605.00834v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The algebraic diversity framework generalizes temporal averaging over multiple observations to algebraic group action on a single observation for second-order statistical estimation. The central open problem in this framework is $\textit{group selection}$: given an $M$-dimensional observation with unknown covariance structure, find the finite group whose spectral decomposition best matches the covariance. Naive enumeration of all subgroups of the symmetric group $S_M$ requires exponential time in $M$. We prove that this combinatorial problem, restricted to a basis of $d$ candidate generators, reduces to a generalized eigenvalue problem derived from the double commutator of the covariance matrix, with complexity $O(d^2M^2 + d^3)$ for sparse (permutation-type) generators and $O(d^2M^3 + d^3)$ in general. The minimum eigenvector gives the optimal generator in the span of the basis in closed form, with no iterative optimization. The minimum eigenvalue is zero if and only if a generator in the span commutes exactly with the covariance, and its magnitude is a certifiable optimality gap otherwise. The problem does not appear in the standard catalog of Garey and Johnson (1979) and links group theory, matrix analysis, and statistical estimation. We relate it to independent component analysis (JADE), structured matrix nearness, and simultaneous diagonalization, and show that the double-commutator form is the unique objective, up to scale, built from a unitarily invariant quadratic norm of the commutator. We extend the framework to non-Abelian symmetry recovery via a Sequential GEVP with deflation, which is sound but not always complete, give canonical generator sets whose direct testing is complete for five named group families, and add two identifiability theorems on the commutant-lattice ambiguity and on whether $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathbf{R})$ recovers a generative subgroup or only a supergroup.
item.dc:creator: Mitchell A. Thornton

item.title: Carbon-Aware Age of Information Scheduling in IoT Networks
item.description: arXiv:2605.21328v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Ensuring timely information delivery while reducing environmental impact is a fundamental challenge in future large-scale 6G and beyond Internet of Things (IoT) deployments. Information timeliness is typically measured using the Age of Information (AoI) metric, whereas environmental impact is often characterized by the Carbon Footprint (CF), which depends on both energy consumption and the Carbon Intensity (CI), defined as the amount of CO$_2$-equivalent emissions produced per unit of consumed energy. Because CI varies over time, minimizing energy consumption alone does not necessarily minimize CF: transmitting the same status update at different times may result in different carbon costs. To address this challenge, we propose Sustainable Age-of-Information Scheduling for IoT Hardware-Constrained Edge Networks (SAOITHE), a scalable scheduling heuristic inspired by Whittle-index decomposition. A closed-form index is derived for a relaxed infinite-horizon single-source model with immediate transmission and unit AoI reset; this index is subsequently used as a priority rule for the original finite-horizon, multi-source system with buffered gateway and server dynamics. Using real-world CI traces across low-, medium-, and high-CI regions, the proposed heuristic operates within the allocated CF and duty-cycle budgets in all evaluated configurations and achieves lower average AoI than baseline policies. The AoI reduction relative to Round Robin is approximately 25% and 20% in low- and medium-CI regions, respectively, and up to 75% in high-CI settings, while maintaining quasilinear per-slot computational complexity.
item.dc:creator: Shih-Kai Chou, Maice Costa, Mihael Mohor\v{c}i\v{c}, Jernej Hribar

item.title: The generalized method of moments is (almost) statistically efficient in low-SNR Gaussian latent-variable models
item.description: arXiv:2605.30095v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study estimation in the low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) regime for a broad class of Gaussian latent-variable models, including Gaussian mixtures and orbit-recovery problems. We show that, in this regime, the generalized method-of-moments (GMoM) matches the first-order asymptotic efficiency of maximum likelihood. In particular, if the moment features are chosen up to the minimal local order required for identification and are weighted optimally, then the resulting GMoM estimator has the same leading asymptotic covariance as the maximum-likelihood estimator. We further show that this efficiency can be achieved using practical, data-driven weighting schemes and is preserved under a broad class of simpler weighting choices, including the commonly used identity-weighted method of moments, although these may incur larger higher-order efficiency losses. On the other hand, inappropriate weighting or discarding moment entries can lead to persistent efficiency losses even as SNR tends to zero, despite preserving identifiability. These results distinguish the moments required for identifiability from those needed for statistical efficiency, and characterize when moment-based estimation can match the performance of maximum likelihood.
item.dc:creator: Amnon Balanov, Tamir Bendory, Dan Edidin

item.title: Probabilistic Risk Sensitivity and Loss Aversion in Cumulative Prospect Theory
item.description: arXiv:2606.06652v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper develops a binary-gamble framework for characterizing risk sensitivity and loss aversion in Cumulative Prospect Theory (CPT). The proposed probabilistic risk-sensitivity metric is defined as a probability-threshold ratio that determines acceptance and preference thresholds in choice problems involving either a certain outcome and a binary gamble or two binary gambles. We show how standard notions of symmetric and non-symmetric bet aversion can be recovered within this framework, and we compare the resulting threshold-based conditions with utility premia, probability premia, and Arrow-Pratt curvature measures. The analysis clarifies when these criteria coincide and when they diverge, particularly for increasing aversion conditions, binary gambles with unequal probability distributions, and settings involving probability weighting functions. We also identify technical restrictions that arise when CPT-utility functions are used to represent loss aversion at the reference point. The resulting framework provides a decision-theoretic interpretation of risk sensitivity that is directly tied to probability thresholds and complements existing premium-based approaches.
item.dc:creator: Symeon Vaidanis, Marios Kountouris

item.title: Breadth-First Search in Succinct Planar Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2607.06221v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: An encoding for a graph class $\mathcal{G}$ is called succinct if it uses $Z_{\mathcal{G}}(n)+o(Z_{\mathcal{G}}(n))$ bits, where $Z_{\mathcal{G}}(n)$ is the information-theoretic minimum number of bits needed to distinguish between $n$-vertex graphs of $\mathcal{G}$; it is called compact if it uses $O(Z_{\mathcal{G}}(n))$ bits. For planar graphs, $Z_{\mathcal{G}}(n)=\Theta(n)$. We present a succinct encoding of planar graphs that supports executing a breadth-first search directly on the encoding. The succinct encoding can be constructed in expected $O(n)$ time using $O(n)$ bits during construction; a compact variant can be constructed in deterministic $O(n)$ time using $O(n)$ bits. Once the encoding is constructed, a BFS from any start vertex can be computed in $O(n)$ time using $o(n)$ additional bits, including the space needed to represent the BFS tree. The resulting BFS tree $T$ remains available for standard tree operations, such as traversal, parent and child queries, layer queries, and lowest common ancestor queries, in constant time per query and amortized constant time per output element. The encoding also supports standard graph queries. Finally, all BFS and tree-query results generalize to separable graph classes, with graph-class-specific construction time and space for the encoding.
item.dc:creator: Johannes Meintrup

item.title: Non-Square UPA-Enabled XL-MIMO Systems: Anisotropic Near-Field Characterization, Fundamental Limits, and Channel Estimation
item.description: arXiv:2607.18736v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) is crucial for next-generation communication systems. In practice, the deployment of non-square uniform planar arrays (UPAs) fundamentally alters wavefront characteristics and induces anisotropic beamfocusing capability along different axes due to the aperture disparity originating from the non-square array geometry. To fully uncover the performance impact of such non-square geometry and thus unleash the potential of the non-square UPAs, we investigate the anisotropic near-field characteristics, fundamental limits, and channel estimation for non-square UPA-enabled XL-MIMO systems. First, we derive the effective beamfocusing distances for the long and short axes of the array. Interestingly, the radiation space of a non-square UPA can be partitioned into three regions, i.e., the fully near-field, the anisotropic near-field, and the far-field regions, and the anisotropic region asymptotically dominates the overall near-field space as the array aspect ratio increases. Then, the asymptotic effective degree of freedom for non-square UPA-enabled XL-MIMO systems is provided, which reveals that distance-domain multiplexing is governed by the long-axis aperture in the large array aspect ratio regime. Furthermore, the closed-form Cramer-Rao bound for distance estimation and the three-dimensional (3D) position error bound (PEB) are derived to reveal the geometry-induced performance trade-offs among distance, azimuth, and elevation estimation, based on which the optimal array aspect ratio that minimizes the 3D PEB is determined. Finally, by exploiting the anisotropic wavefront properties, we design a 3D anisotropic near-field codebook to facilitate low-complexity channel estimation for non-square UPAs. Numerical results validate that the proposed codebook achieves comparable accuracy to the 3D polar-domain codebook at reduced complexity.
item.dc:creator: Yilong Liu, Xi Yang, Jing Xu, Jun Zhang, Shi jin

item.title: Neilson's Weak vs. Strong Loss Aversion: A Characterization and a Generalized CPT-Utility Function
item.description: arXiv:2607.22085v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In multi-objective and multi-criteria decision-making under risk, especially in settings involving individual behavior, risk-aware analysis based on subjective evaluation has become increasingly important. Moving beyond risk-neutral modeling and the constraints of Expected Utility Theory (EUT), Cumulative Prospect Theory (CPT) provides a behaviorally grounded framework for capturing how individuals perceive and evaluate risky prospects. This paper conducts a rigorous theoretical analysis of Neilson's definitions of aversion. We provide a gamble-based interpretation, sharpen key conceptual distinctions, and make explicit the conditions under which the weak and strong notions coincide as well as when they diverge. Furthermore, we examine the Kobberling-Wakker utility function and related standard CPT specifications, highlighting structural limitations and inconsistencies that arise when these forms are required to satisfy Neilson-type aversion conditions. To address these issues, we propose a generalized CPT-utility function that retains the canonical reference-dependent shape while offering additional flexibility. This generalization extends the descriptive scope of CPT and provides an explicit functional form that is useful for sensitivity analysis and utility function-based optimization.
item.dc:creator: Symeon Vaidanis, Marios Kountouris

item.title: A complete characterization of sequential testability and change detectability in i.i.d. models
item.description: arXiv:2609.05752v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give qualitative and quantitative necessary and sufficient conditions for sequential testing and change detection in an i.i.d. composite problem. A level-\(\alpha\) test with power one against every alternative exists if and only if the alternatives are separated from the null by a countable family of finite-block events. Equivalent conditions use randomized tests, bounded scores, e-processes, reduced-filtration test supermartingales, and a countable cover with positive finite-block weak-$*$ convex-hull separation. The construction gives pointwise expected sample size \(O_Q(\log(1/\alpha))\). Quantitatively, one e-process attains the intrinsic pointwise growth rate \(\Gamma(Q)\) at every alternative if and only if a countable family of bounded block bets recovers these rates. The same condition characterizes simultaneous attainment of the sharp expected-sample-size coefficient \(1/\Gamma(Q)\); arbitrary attainable lower rate profiles admit an analogous characterization. Total-variation separability of the alternatives suffices for recovery. Weak lower semicontinuity of the KL projection, in particular weak compactness of the null, also identifies \(\Gamma(Q)\) with \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathrm{KL}(Q\|P)\). The qualitative and quantitative conditions also characterize change detectability under fixed-time false-alarm bounds \(\Prob_{P^\infty}(T_\gamma\le n)\le n/\gamma\), together with ordinary ARL control. Whenever countable rate recovery holds, for any \(\eta>0\) one calibrated e-detector has robust Lorden delay asymptotic to \((\log\gamma)/\Gamma(Q)\) at finite positive rates, while satisfying the stronger optional-horizon inequality and placing every null ARL in \([\gamma,(1+\eta)\gamma+1]\). Examples exhibit a strict cost of simultaneous optimality and show that ordinary ARL alone supports neither characterization, even with finite, tightly calibrated null means.

item.title: The LQ Digital Mode Family: Protocol Architecture and Reference Specification for Weak-Signal Communications
item.description: arXiv:2609.06427v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper introduces LQ8, an open-source weak-signal digital mode for amateur radio that completes structured two-way contacts in 4 transmissions (60 s), achieving a 1.50x speedup over canonical 6-transmission exchanges (90 s) and 1.25x over 5-transmission RR73 exchanges (75 s) while preserving complete bidirectional exchange of Maidenhead grid locators, signal reports, and mutual acknowledgments. By replacing fixed-width message-type headers with variable-length prefix codes matched to physical-layer bit budgets, LQ8 packs the answering station's grid locator and measured signal report into a single 77-bit reply. In multi-station pileup operations, LQ8 confirms up to two answering stations simultaneously within a single-carrier 50.0 Hz transmission with a 0.0 dB RF power-splitting penalty, achieving a peak rate of 240 QSOs/h in continuous pileup (4x over single-carrier FT8; 480 QSOs/h dual-carrier) while retaining -21.0 dB SNR sensitivity. The protocol family also defines three extended profiles (LQ16, LQ4, and LQ2) tailored for extreme sensitivity, VHF/UHF contesting, and fast-burst channels.

item.title: OSFP4: Joint Optimization of Diagonal Smoothing and Block Scales for NVFP4 Quantization
item.description: arXiv:2610.08231v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: NVFP4 is an attractive datatype for large language model (LLM) inference, offering compact storage and native tensor-core acceleration. However, preserving accuracy using NVFP4 requires careful quantization. In this work we develop a novel quantization scheme called Optimized Smoothing and Scaling for NVFP4 (OSFP4). For each linear projection it uses a diagonal smoothing matrix whose entries are optimized to minimize the squared matrix-product quantization error under NVFP4, taking into account the rounding procedure that is used (either round-to-nearest, or GPTQ-style successive interference cancellation). This requires performing joint optimization on the smoothing entries as well as the block scales, which is facilitated by analyzing a multiplicative-dither FP4 quantizer instead of the fixed deterministic one. Experiments show that OSFP4 achieves the highest average accuracy among the evaluated competitors in the corresponding quantization settings, while retaining approximately 94-97\% of vendor NVFP4 prefill throughput on the measured workloads. Our code is available in https://github.com/neriahbd/OSFP4

item.title: Diffusion Models are Provably Efficient Priors for Sparse Recovery
item.description: arXiv:2611.24602v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Diffusion models have transformed generative modeling through their ability to capture and generate samples from complex data distributions. This success has spurred substantial interest in using pretrained diffusion models as expressive priors for highly ill-posed inverse problems in imaging and sensing. Despite strong empirical performance, theoretical understanding of this approach remains limited: existing guarantees are often asymptotic or entail prohibitive computational costs in the worst case. In this paper, we address this gap by studying sparse recovery from a small number of linear measurements, a classical problem in compressed sensing. We show that, given an accurate diffusion model capturing a sparsity-promoting Bernoulli-Gaussian prior, a likelihood-guided annealed Langevin sampler provably recovers the sparse signal in polynomial time with near-optimal sample complexity for a broad family of random and deterministic sensing matrices. When the signal is indeed drawn from the postulated prior, we further establish total variation guarantees for posterior sampling after a final denoising step. These results lay a theoretical foundation for statistically and computationally efficient inverse solvers with diffusion priors.

item.title: Entanglement Geometry Beyond Polygons: Graph-Theoretic Entanglement Inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2611.25019v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Entanglement entropies of pure multipartite states can be constrained by organizing subsystem cuts as edges (hyperedges) of graphs (hypergraphs). Starting from the one-party entanglement polygon inequality, we derive these constraints from strong subadditivity and pure-state complementarity, with optimal coefficients and explicit equality conditions. Our central result determines, for a distinguished two-party cut and an arbitrary weighted family of cuts, the optimal polygon coefficient: the smallest total weight of the cuts separating a member of the distinguished pair from a remaining party. A refinement involving three mutual information terms gives the exact minimum of the weighted sum at fixed entropies of the two parties and of their union, attained by at most three independent bipartite pure states. The analogous coefficient is also optimal for a distinguished one-party cut and for any distinguished cut that the family does not split. This criterion recovers the cycle and complete-graph inequalities and shows that uniform incidence parity, which we prove sufficient for polygon inequalities on hypergraphs, is not necessary. Averaging strong subadditivity over both sides of a bipartition gives a sharp $k$-marginal inequality with coefficient $2\binom{n-2}{k-1}$, and we determine uniformly optimal coefficients for collective hyperstar inequalities. For paths and overlapping hyperchains, the deficits are exact sums of conditional mutual information terms; genuinely multipartite entangled cluster states saturate the hyperchain inequality while the chain inequality remains strict. We characterize pure chain equality states, bound the trace distance to cycle equality states independently of the number of parties and local dimensions, and obtain bond-dimension bounds for matrix product states and sequential-recovery error estimates.
